question: Of 39 site-level records, how many are actually surveyed in both 2001 and 2005, and is there any geographically validated off–Ross-Island sample for interpreting Royds' distinct iceberg-era trajectory?
comparison_grains: publisher geographic parent descriptor with islands/regions explicitly not considered independent island units
planned_direct_evidence: Require source 2001 and 2005 both genuine nonblank numeric values in same literal census site row; no missing-to-zero or interpolation
Separate 2001/2005 matched cohort with exact source geographic name (V16 33/39) from sites with no linked official geography
List source parent descriptor but do not equate peninsulas, archipelagos, regional labels with individual geographic islands
Compute 2001 and 2005 reported counts and direction of change only for actually paired records; no causal migration/individual survival
Report matched Ross Island source units vs all geography-identified off-Ross sites, and source-counts with unknown geographic mapping
Report pooled change only as exploratory descriptive and not as causal control; sampling and provenance might overlap earlier Lyver 2014 Ross studies
Refuse a pseudo-DID using 1999 because 1999 sources cover ONLY Ross Island, and do not fabricate 2024 off–Ross counts
prior_art_veto: Dugger et al 2010 PNAS 10.1073/pnas.1000623107 shows iceberg-era adult dispersal up to 3.5% versus usual below 1%
LaRue et al 2013 PLOS ONE doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0060548 already shows Beaufort glacier retreat and reduced post-2005 visits to Ross Island
Lyver et al 2014 PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0091188 already analyses Ross Sea 1981–2012 population dynamics and regional synchrony
Original NZ 2026 census may overlap same survey counts, not an independent iceberg-era natural experiment.
success_for_novel_causal_test_requires: independent externally dated physical ice access per site and season
confirmed source/recipient marked birds and actual prospecting or egg attempt
at least two event/region replicated contemporaneous and predisturbance site-year comparisons
effort-aligned detection and chicks rather than pair-only census
